text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000351 bills 99215 far above what its patient complexity predicts, with much of it on low-complexity patients, but the few charts returned all support the billed levels, so documentation is too thin to judge.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern because the 99215 excess appears across every complexity tier, including patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Sampled examples include C0190858, C0190898 and C0190900, which carry only symptom codes such as rash or upper respiratory infection, while the high-complexity examples (C0190802, C0190873) fit the expected picture. Against that, the four documented 99215 charts (including low-complexity C0190883 and C0190964) were all recorded at high MDM, and no documented claim at any level fell below the billed code. Only 1 of 11 moderate-or-higher data-reviewed notes lacked a lab or test line, so there is little sign of inflated notes. With records for only about a tenth of claims and just four 99215 charts, the sample cannot confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity decision-making or templated or cloned language."}
